newsitem.title: USA: Pratt wins Asiana Airlines engine contract.
newsitem.headline: Pratt wins Asiana Airlines engine contract.

text.p: Pratt & Whitney, a unit of United Technologies Corp., said Monday it won a contract from South Korea's Asiana Airlines to provide engines for 48 new twin-engine Airbus Industrie A330 and Boeing 777 aircraft.
Pratt & Whitney gave no figure for the value of the deal.
But a Pratt spokesman said it includes more than 100 engines, including spares, and industry analysts said each engine costs an average of about $10 million.
Pratt's PW4000 engine family will power all of the aircraft. The engines will be delivered between 1998 and 2006.
The plan calls for 18 firm orders and 10 options for Airbus Industrie A330 widebody aircraft, Pratt said. Asiana has 15 firm orders for Boeing 777 widebody aircraft and five options.
Before 1996, Asiana relied exclusively on General Electric Co. engines to power its aircraft, Pratt said.

The new contract boosts Pratt's 1996 market share to 70 percent on the A330 and 43 percent on the Boeing 777. Overall, Pratt engines are found on 42 percent of Boeing 777s and 53 percent of A330s, it said.
United Technologies stock rose 75 cents to $65 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
